A1.justification: Both PDFs describe System-Embedded Diffusion Bridge Models. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched reliably despite additions and relocation in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments across four datasets in Table 2, system-misspecification evaluations, and appendix hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds reconstruction benchmarks, robustness experiments, schedule ablations, runtime measurements and additional baseline evaluations.

M1.justification: The core linear SDB dynamics, training loss and sampling algorithm remain unchanged. V2 develops the previously sketched nonlinear extension into an estimation-then-Jacobian procedure (C.2/E.4) and applies a regularized pseudoinverse for deblurring (E.3), constituting limited adaptations.

E1.justification: V2 retains the four original dataset-task pairs and adds Flowers102 motion deblurring and CIFAR10 nonlinear contrast recovery. Additional test scenarios include enlarged downsampling kernels, JPEG corruption and Poisson-noise CT/MRI, substantially broadening the evaluated measurement conditions.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds UNSB and SBF as evaluated unpaired-data baselines for MRI reconstruction. The original supervised and plug-and-play comparator sets remain unchanged; IRSDE in the new tables corresponds to the existing IR-SDE baseline.

E3.justification: The original training budgets, sampling steps and reconstruction metrics are retained. Added protocols include 128×128 deblurring, specified Poisson-intensity sweeps, quadratic/cosine schedule configurations, and operation-level CT timing over four batches of eight. These are new experimental settings, not revisions to the original comparison.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained CT/MRI parameter-shift and hyperparameter analyses, v2 adds severe operator/noise mismatch tests, ill-conditioned-operator evaluation, VP/VE noise-schedule ablations, and computational-overhead analysis (E.2–E.7). These investigate several previously untested robustness and efficiency questions.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies seed-based uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing hyperparameter boxplots are retained. V2's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical-significance reporting but introduces no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 is unchanged apart from equivalent CT FID rounding. New tables substantially expand reported outcomes: deblurring PSNR is 30.39 for SDB versus 29.74 for DDBM (Table 6). Rankings are not uniformly favorable: at MRI Poisson intensity 12, I2SB has lower FID than SDB, 38.1304 versus 38.1484 (Table 5).

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 3 asserting asymptotically exact posterior sampling, supported by four lemmas in A.3. It also adds a commutativity argument in A.4 and computational-complexity analysis in E.7. Selected noise factors in Equation 9 gain square roots; the earlier main derivations remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central system-embedded bridge and generalization claims. Section 6 changes nonlinear applicability from an unvalidated possibility to a demonstrated, preliminary treatment restricted to differentiable systems, modestly extending the claimed demonstrated scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix F develops range-guided synthesis explanations and a substantive perception-distortion interpretation of the retained superresolution results, including a suggestion of proximity to a Pareto frontier. V2 also adds interpretations of schedule tradeoffs, practical overhead and nonlinear applicability.

D1.justification: New implementation information includes Tikhonov/Wiener pseudoinverse approximation, five gradient-descent initialization steps, analytic Jacobians/Jacobian-vector products, and operator-based computation. Original optimizer settings, checkpoint selection, A100 hardware, training-time disclosures and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds literature connections for unpaired Schrödinger bridges, perception-distortion tradeoffs, subspace diffusion and flow matching, alongside new dataset citations. It removes the GAN-inversion example and its Creswell–Bharath citation. The principal supervised-versus-plug-and-play positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Targeted rewrites expand nonlinear explanations and the experimental overview; pseudocode moves into the main text, appendix sections are reorganized, and acknowledgments and a conference checklist are added.

P2.justification: V2 adds nine appendix tables, Tables 3–11, displaying new comparisons, ablations, complexity and runtime. Both algorithms move into the main text with explanatory comments. Existing Figures 1–9 retain their visual content, and the original tables retain their basic structure.

improvement.justification: The new stress tests, schedule ablations and runtime measurements strengthen practical evidence beyond v1's parameter sweeps. However, C.2's stated nonlinear observation model omits the affine offset present in Equation 26, and A.3's singular-covariance whitening does not explain how noiseless measurement information is preserved. These gaps, overgeneralized ranking summaries and continued absence of uncertainty estimates limit the overall gain despite the substantial empirical expansion.
